verdicts.reason: The diff touches only three src files; grep for OptimizedCursorPaginator / optimized_pagination / enable_advanced_features across the whole checkout returns hits only in src/, none in tests/, and neither existing test file exercises the new class, the new query param, or a negative-offset cursor through BasePaginator.

OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged (copied from the numeric Paginator), while DateTimePaginator converts with datetime.fromtimestamp(...)/multiplier; BasePaginator.build_queryset then splices that value into a raw SQL `datetime <= %s` extra-where (paginator.py:110-124) against a DateTimeField, so a page-2 cursor feeds an integer into a timestamp comparison.
The same diff defines `class OptimizedCursorPaginator(BasePaginator)` in src/sentry/api/paginator.py, so the import at organization_auditlogs.py:11 resolves; the class is broken, but it exists.

Same defect as c002 with the correct prescribed fix: DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor does datetime.fromtimestamp(float(cursor.value)/multiplier), the new class does not, and build_queryset injects the value into a SQL comparison against the datetime column. Note the path is masked in practice because get_item_key blows up first (see c005).

get_item_key does math.floor/ceil directly on getattr(item, 'datetime'), copied from the numeric Paginator instead of DateTimePaginator's strftime conversion; build_cursor calls key(results[0]) (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:377, 439), so any non-empty result set on the optimized path raises TypeError on a datetime.

All three sub-assertions check out: BasePaginator is shared by Paginator/DateTimePaginator (30+ DateTimePaginator call sites alone); line 182 clamps only when `not cursor.is_prev`, leaving the is_prev branch unclamped (a hazard that pre-dates the PR — the base previously used the raw offset in both directions — but the diff rewrites exactly that line); line 192 still compares against the un-clamped `offset`; and OffsetPaginator/MergingOffsetPaginator raise BadPaginationError('Pagination offset cannot be negative') where the new clamp silently returns page one.

RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None` and is documented as None when the user_id has no membership; ControlSiloOrganizationEndpoint.convert_args passes user_id=request.user.id, and ApiKey/OrgAuthToken auth resolves request.user to AnonymousUser (authentication.py transform_auth line 167-168), so member is None and the attribute access raises. One correction to the claim: line 71 runs unconditionally, before the `use_optimized` check, so it crashes on every request from such a caller, not only when optimized_pagination=true — i.e. it breaks an endpoint that worked before.

The branch's own comments claim both 'efficient traversal in both directions' and 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds', while reverse paging already exists via cursor.is_prev in BasePaginator; and the branch cannot deliver either because Django raises ValueError on a negative slice start. The assertion is checkable and correct, not a bare question.

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a line-for-line copy of BasePaginator.get_result (cursor default, limit clamp, build_queryset, max_hits/count_hits, extra, prev trimming, build_cursor, post_query_filter) with only the negative-offset branch added, minus the base's explanatory comments; the base's own clamp fix at line 182 is already duplicated at line 884.

The base version of the endpoint has no statsPeriod/start/end handling at all — AuditLogQueryParamSerializer only declares `event` and `actor`, and the diff removes nothing from it. There is no such regression.
Same defect as c002/c004 stated compactly: the raw integer cursor value is appended as a param to an `extra(where=["...datetime <= %s"])` clause on a timestamptz column.

Verified with grep -P '[ \t]+$' and cat -A: trailing whitespace on four added lines, three consecutive blank lines before `class OptimizedCursorPaginator`, and a blank line at EOF. .pre-commit-config.yaml runs black and flake8, and setup.cfg's extend-ignore does not cover W291/W293/E303/W391.

Each quoted comment is contradicted by the code: Django raises ValueError on negative slice bounds rather than 'handling boundary conditions'; the queryset is filtered only by organization_id, so nothing about permissions makes an out-of-bounds offset safe; and the endpoint's 'authorized administrators' gate is the weak check described in c014.

OrganizationMember.has_global_access is BooleanField(default=True) and is never assigned False anywhere in src/ (only in tests/), so for any member who already passes OrganizationAuditPermission's org:write requirement the gate is unconditionally true; request.user.is_superuser is the raw DB flag rather than is_active_superuser(request), which the endpoint's own permission class uses. Minor imprecision: is_active_superuser appears in OrganizationAuditPermission and convert_args, not 'two lines away' in this file.

AuditLogQueryParamSerializer declares only event/actor and DRF silently ignores unknown input keys, so optimized_pagination is read straight off request.GET with a case-sensitive == "true"; 'True', '1', 'yes' fall through to the default paginator with no 400 and no signal to the caller.

Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.') for a negative slice start (Django >=5.2 per requirements-base.txt), so `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with the deliberately negative start is an unconditional 500; the cursor offset is fully user-controlled via Cursor.from_string (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:57-66) with no validation, and ValueError is not caught by paginate's BadPaginationError handler.
No test in the checkout references optimized_pagination or constructs a cursor for this endpoint; the existing audit-log tests only cover the default DateTimePaginator path.

The only change to cursors.py is two comment lines above `self.offset = int(offset)`; Cursor gained no negative-offset logic, and int(offset) accepted negative values before this PR as well, so the comment describes a behaviour change that did not happen here.

The diff contains no benchmark, profile, issue reference or query plan, and the paginator it replaces is the same keyset scheme (build_queryset adds a `datetime <= %s` bound rather than a large OFFSET), so the claimed performance win is unsupported by anything in the change.
